findings.title: legacy dispatch command panics with not-implemented stub
findings.note: legacyHandler is registered in the live command dispatch table (reachable via Run/os.Args), not an abstract interface method, so invoking the "legacy" command crashes the process instead of returning an error.

findings.title: Fetch has no timeout and can hang forever on health check
findings.note: http.Get uses http.DefaultClient which has no Timeout set, so if the remote never responds this call in main() blocks indefinitely with no way to cancel.

findings.title: Deprecated Fetch left in place and still called from main
findings.note: Marker is 671 days old with no ticket referenced, and the replacement (FetchWithTimeout) exists in httpc_safe.go but the deprecated call site in main.go was never migrated.

looks_bad_but_fine.why: payments.killswitch is a documented, ticketed (runbook-referenced) deliberate deferral toggle, not an unfinished stub.
Builder pattern with chained With* methods is a complete, intentional API, not a half-finished contract.

not_assessed: test coverage or flakiness of store_test.go
whether internal/crypto md5 use or internal/shell exec.Command represent security vulnerabilities (different debt family, not assessed here)
